problem_type: Credential material presence conflated with enablement and verification
symptom: After an offline key save the UI says saved and not verified, but the persisted vendor projection reports hasApiKey=false, so model listing and generation treat the credential as missing.
direct_cause: credentialRecordCounts rejected records with enabled=false, and apiKeyDecryptStatus therefore returned missing for pending offline records.
class_root: The credential record used one enabled boolean for two different facts: whether key material exists and whether the credential is currently enabled/verified.
affected_population: Any probe-based vendor saved while network validation is inconclusive
Windows, macOS, or Linux users reopening a persisted pending credential
Every catalog reader that consumes the hasApiKey projection
entry_points: Catalog persistence projection derives hasApiKey from credential material and decrypt status.
Catalog availability checks enablement separately before decrypting or probing.
The key-only page maps pending, published, and saved facts to shared bilingual copy keys.
internal_only_reason: This is an application-level credential lifecycle invariant owned by the local catalog; Electron safeStorage remains unchanged and no provider protocol is being changed.
invariants: A non-empty persisted key record remains visible as saved even when enabled=false and verificationPending=true.
A disabled credential is never decrypted or probed for model availability until the promotion boundary enables it.
The UI says saved and not verified for pending material and does not turn that state into no key.

door_reduction.why_not: The 19 hasApiKey readers are presentation, health, onboarding, and generation consumers that must continue to consume the single catalog projection; merging them would recreate parallel facts. The two credentialRecordCounts occurrences are the shared material/status and availability boundaries: the first owns material status, the second owns the explicit enabled gate, so both responsibilities must remain explicit. The copy-key type is a renderer boundary that keeps bilingual state mapping in one owner.

generality_proof: All checked readers receive the same Vendor projection from readCatalog, while all model availability checks converge on createCatalogAvailability. Making credentialRecordCounts material-only and keeping enabled as an explicit availability gate covers pending records regardless of vendor, caller, platform, or persisted run.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Identify persisted key material without interpreting enablement or verification state.
Keep disabled credentials out of decrypt/probe and feed the shared availability owner.
Project hasApiKey and credentialVerificationPending once for every renderer and main-process reader.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The offline walk reads this persisted projection after reopening the page; it now sees hasApiKey=true for decryptable pending material.
The same pending record remains unusable while disabled, and the boundary avoids decrypt/probe until promotion.
The page consumes hasApiKey and credentialVerificationPending through the shared copy resolver, so saved pending material is rendered as saved and not verified.
Health probing continues to consume the main-process hasApiKey projection; request construction is intentionally outside this remediation line.

recurrence.reason: Every network-inconclusive save can create enabled=false, verificationPending=true, and the same projection would previously misclassify it as missing.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs credentialRecordCounts -> secrets.ts and catalogModelAvailability.ts
rg -n hasApiKey electron src tests -> onboarding, health, generation, and recovery consumers

prevention.invariant: Material presence is independent from enablement; disabled records are not probed, while pending material remains visible in the catalog projection.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing material returns missing; locked or legacy material keeps its explicit decrypt status; disabled material remains unavailable without being relabeled as absent by the projection.
prevention.strategy: Keep one material predicate and one availability gate at the shared catalog boundary; all readers consume their respective owner instead of rebuilding the boolean.

legacy_paths.rationale: No legacy writer or migration path is removed; existing persisted records keep their shape and are interpreted with separated material and availability facts.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in the application catalog invariant; Electron safeStorage and provider request dependencies are unchanged.

migration: No on-disk migration is needed. Existing records already contain apiKey, enabled, and optional verificationPending; only their projection and availability interpretation change.
residual_risks: The parallel F-vendorhealth2 line may change custom relay authorization-header precedence; this remediation deliberately does not alter verification request construction.
A pending credential remains unavailable until the existing revalidation/promotion path enables it; the UI now states that boundary explicitly.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The secrets boundary defines whether persisted material exists; catalog availability then owns the separate enablement gate before any model reader can use it.
